-D Proof of Theorem 1

In order to prove Lemma 1, we need to resort the following lemma, in which upper bounds of kernel metrics between two nominal states and between an actual state and the nominal one are derived:

Lemma 9.

Given the training dataset 𝒟N={𝒟N,i}i=1nx\mathcal{D}_{N}=\{\mathcal{D}_{N,i}\}^{n_{x}}_{i=1}, and let Assumption 1 hold. Then, the kernel metrics between two nominal states are given by

di​(f^​(x1,u,𝒟N),f^​(x2,u,𝒟N))≤ζ^N,i​(x1,x2),\displaystyle d_{i}(\hat{{f}}({x}_{1},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}),\hat{{f}}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}))\leq\hat{\zeta}_{N,i}({x}_{1},{x}_{2}), (86)

for all x1,x2∈ℝnxx_{1},x_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{x}}, u∈ℝnuu\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{u}}, and i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}, where

ζ^N,i​(x1,x2)=2​αi2​{1−exp⁡(−12​‖b⊙d⁡(x1,x2)‖Λx,i−12)}\displaystyle\hat{\zeta}_{N,i}({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=\sqrt{2\alpha_{i}^{2}\left\{1-\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\|{b}\odot{d}({x}_{1},{x}_{2})\|^{2}_{\Lambda_{x,i}^{-1}}\right)\right\}} (87)

with d=[d1,…,dnx]⊤d=[d_{1},\ldots,d_{n_{x}}]^{\top}. Moreover, the kernel metrics between an actual state and the nominal one are given by

di​(f⁡(x1,u)+w,f^​(x2,u,𝒟N))≤ζN,i​(x1,x2,u),\displaystyle d_{i}({f}({x}_{1},{u})+{w},\hat{{f}}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}))\leq\zeta_{N,i}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},{u}), (88)

for all x1,x2∈ℝnxx_{1},x_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{x}}, u∈ℝnuu\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{u}}, and i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}, where

ζN,i​(x1,x2,u)\displaystyle\zeta_{N,i}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},{u})
=2​αi2​{1−exp⁡(−12​‖b⊙d⁡(x1,x2)+δN​(x2,u)‖Λx,i−12)}\displaystyle=\sqrt{2\alpha_{i}^{2}\left\{1-\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\|{b}\odot{d}({x}_{1},{x}_{2})+\delta_{N}(x_{2},u)\|^{2}_{\Lambda_{x,i}^{-1}}\right)\right\}} (89)

with d=[d1,…,dnx]⊤d=[d_{1},\ldots,d_{n_{x}}]^{\top} and δN=[δN,1,…,δN,nx]⊤\delta_{N}=[\delta_{N,1},\ldots,\delta_{N,n_{x}}]^{\top}. □\Box

(proof of Lemma 9): Given the training dataset 𝒟N={𝒟N,i}i=1nx\mathcal{D}_{N}=\{\mathcal{D}_{N,i}\}_{i=1}^{n_{x}}, from the definition of (11), the kernel metric between the two nominal states f^​(x1,u,𝒟N)\hat{f}({x}_{1},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}) and f^​(x2,u,𝒟N)\hat{f}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}) can be computed by

=2​αi2−2​𝗄x,i​(f^​(x1,u,𝒟N,i),f^​(x2,u,𝒟N))\displaystyle=\sqrt{2\alpha_{i}^{2}-2\mathsf{k}_{x,i}(\hat{{f}}({x}_{1},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N,i}),\hat{{f}}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}))}

≤2αi2{1−exp(−12∑j=1nx1λi,jx|bi⋅di(x1,x2)|2)}\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{2\alpha_{i}^{2}\left\{1-\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_{x}}\frac{1}{\lambda^{x}_{i,j}}|b_{i}\cdot d_{i}({x}_{1},{x}_{2})|^{2}\right)\right\}}

for all i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}. In the similar way as the above, the upper bound of the kernel metric between the actual state f⁡(x1,u)+w{f}({x}_{1},{u})+{w} and the nominal one f^​(x2,u,𝒟N)\hat{{f}}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N}) can be computed by

for all i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}. Moreover, from Lemma 1 and Lemma 2, we then have

|fi​(x1,u)+wi−f^i​(x2,u,𝒟N,i)|\displaystyle|f_{i}({x}_{1},{u})+w_{i}-\hat{f}_{i}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N,i})|
≤|fi​(x1,u)−fi​(x2,u)|+|fi​(x2,u)−f^i​(x2,u,𝒟N,i)|+σwi\displaystyle\leq|f_{i}({x}_{1},{u})-f_{i}({x}_{2},{u})|+|f_{i}({x}_{2},{u})-\hat{f}_{i}({x}_{2},{u};\mathcal{D}_{N,i})|+\sigma_{w_{i}}
≤bi⋅di​(x1,x2)+βN,i⋅σfi​(x2,u,𝒟N,i)+σwi,\displaystyle\leq b_{i}\cdot d_{i}({x}_{1},{x}_{2})+\beta_{N,i}\cdot\sigma_{f_{i}}(x_{2},u;\mathcal{D}_{N,i})+\sigma_{w_{i}},

for all i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}. Hence, from (93) and (94), it follows that

for all i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}. □\Box

Hence, if mk=Hk−1m_{k}=H_{k}-1, it follows from (100), Lemma 3, Assumption 2, and x^∗​(Hk|tk)∈𝒳f\hat{x}^{*}(H_{k}|t_{k})\in\mathcal{X}_{f} that x^​(1|tk+1)∈𝒳S\hat{x}(1|t_{k+1})\in\mathcal{X}_{S}. Hence, we can repeat the same procedure as above and the upper bound of the kernel metric between the two nominal state x^​(Hk−mk|tk+1)\hat{x}(H_{k}-m_{k}|t_{k+1}) and x^∗​(Hk|tk)\hat{x}^{*}(H_{k}|t_{k}) is given by

di​(x^​(Hk−mk|tk+1),x^∗​(Hk|tk))≤γi,\displaystyle d_{i}(\hat{x}(H_{k}-m_{k}|t_{k+1}),\hat{x}^{*}(H_{k}|t_{k}))\leq\gamma_{i}, (101)

for all i∈ℕ1:nxi\in\mathbb{N}_{1:n_{x}}, and therefore, x^​(Hk−mk|tk+1)∈𝒳S\hat{x}(H_{k}-m_{k}|t_{k+1})\in\mathcal{X}_{S}. Thus, from Assumption 2, there exists u=C⁡(x^​(Hk−mk|tk+1))u=C(\hat{x}(H_{k}-m_{k}|t_{k+1})), such that x^​(Hk−mk+1|tk+1)=f^​(x^​(Hk−mk|tk+1),u)∈𝒳f\hat{x}(H_{k}-m_{k}+1|t_{k+1})=\hat{f}(\hat{x}(H_{k}-m_{k}|t_{k+1}),u)\in\mathcal{X}_{f}, satisfying the terminal constraint. In other words, the OCP at tk+1t_{k+1} is shown to be feasible with the prediction horizon Hk+1=Hk−mk+1H_{k+1}=H_{k}-m_{k}+1.
∎

Proof.
